card: Reverts the CMake configure check for SetThreadDescription and calls it unconditionally on Windows, while documenting the MinGW-w64 12.0 minimum toolchain requirement and dropping MSVCRT support from the Nix cross-compilation shell. The check was a temporary measure prior to branching 33.x, and master now requires MinGW-w64 >= 12.0 with UCRT. This is an internal build cleanup and documentation update.
changed_since_previous: No functional changes to the diff; the patch contents match the previous revision.
evidence: PR description: "A follow-up reverting #36057, now that we've branched off for `33.x`. Also documents `mingw-w64` requirements (#32380)."
Commit message: "Revert 'build: check for SetThreadDescription() at configure time'"
problem: A CMake probe for SetThreadDescription was temporarily added in #36057 to support older MinGW-w64 versions prior to the 33.x release branch. On master, MinGW-w64 >= 12.0 is now required, making the configure probe obsolete, while the build documentation did not state this minimum version and Nix tooling retained dead MSVCRT configurations.

risk.why: A mistake could break Windows compilation for developers using outdated MinGW-w64 toolchains or misconfigure the Nix development shell.

summary: Reverts the CMake configure check for SetThreadDescription, assuming availability on all Windows builds. Documents the MinGW-w64 12.0 minimum requirement in Windows build guides, and drops legacy MSVCRT build support from the Nix cross-compilation shell in favor of UCRT.
